land.text: northern Tigray and Eritrea, where "a Proto-Aksumite polity had emerged ... by the 4th century BC"

successors.note: The page says "it is not known whether dʿmt ended as a civilization before the Kingdom of Aksum's early stages" and calls Dʿmt's successors "smaller unknown" kingdoms; the Kingdom of Axum row in Cliopatria starts in -50.

capitals.name: Yeha
capitals.note: "the capital of dʿmt may have been present-day Yeha" (a possibility on the page); Mätära is "an additional town and ceremonial centre". Coordinates approximate (Yeha is not in the gazetteer; it lies near Adigrat in northern Tigray).

correction.text: "located in present-day Eritrea and the northern Tigray Region of Ethiopia"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Dʿmt). "located in present-day Eritrea and the northern Tigray Region of Ethiopia"; I draw Tigray and the Eritrean highland provinces, which is wider than the page's "northern Tigray". No area on the page; the Sabaean influence is "minor, limited to a few localities" per some sources and no Arabian territory is drawn.

ledger.note: 8th century BC: the kingdom of Dʿmt appears in Eritrea and northern Tigray. Infobox "Established: 8th c. BC"; "The culture of dʿmt can be dated to approximately 800/700-400 BC"; the page calls a span from the end of the 8th to the 6th century BC "a hypothesis". -750 is a placeholder for the century.

region.text: "located in present-day Eritrea and the northern Tigray Region of Ethiopia"

ledger.note: About 400 BC: Dʿmt ends. Infobox "Disestablished: 4th c. BC"; "a Proto-Aksumite polity had emerged in northern Tégray by the 4th century BC"; the page says it is not known whether Dʿmt ended before Aksum's early stages (the Aksumite kingdom "rose during the first century BC"). The Great Temple at Yeha is "dated ... to around 700 BC" (Yeha page). sources.title: Dʿmt
sources.note: Dates (8th-4th century BC, c. 800/700-400 BC), Yeha as a possible capital, extent (Eritrea and northern Tigray), Sabaean influence, no link to Aksum established.

notes: New dossier, thin by necessity: the Dʿmt page gives only the infobox centuries (8th to 4th BC), a probable capital at Yeha, the extent 'present-day Eritrea and the northern Tigray Region' and Sabaean influence; its four rulers (ʿArky(t)n, Smʿt, Yrʿt, ʿAdt) have no dates, so no ruler strip. Pages opened: Dʿmt, Yeha (2). Both start and end are century placeholders at confidence 1. The 350-year gap between the end of Dʿmt (-400) and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Axum (-50) is the 'Proto-Aksumite' polity, 'smaller unknown kingdoms': a gap-filler should open the Proto-Aksumite / Pre-Aksumite period source. The Axum dossier (af-01-a, kingdom-of-axum) starts at -50; the successor link is the land only. Gazetteer names needed: Yeha (near Adigrat, Tigray; approximate coordinate 14.28 N 39.03 E used), Mätära (Metera, Eritrea).
